messages:
maria (PM): Heads-up — reconciling the Q2 roadmap. Two competing priorities: SOC2 Type II prep (sales is pushing for an audit window) vs a 6-week experiment to validate quantized model performance on Dedicated. Need sequencing guidance. Thoughts?
kevin (Eng): If we prioritize SOC2 now we lock down infra changes; experiments get delayed. But experiments could reduce token costs a lot.
nisha (Security): SOC2 has a hard date from a pilot customer — they need evidence in our control matrix by end of Q2. If we slip, we risk losing the deal.
sam (Product Ops): Can we run the experiment in an isolated tenant and keep audit scope clean? Maybe parallelize with limited headcount.
kevin (Eng): Parallel is possible but non-trivial. Context switching kills throughput. Also audits care about change management — if we change infra mid-audit it's extra work.
alex (Research): From a RICE perspective experiments = Reach: medium, Impact: high on cost, Confidence: low, Effort: medium. SOC2 = Reach: low (single deal), Impact: high revenue/cred, Confidence: high, Effort: high.
maria (PM): OK quick RICE sketch — can folks drop 1-line R/I/C/E numbers? We need something to show execs.
nisha (Security): SOC2: R 1, I 8, C 7, E 6 (out of 10). Critical controls need docs + infra lockdown.
kevin (Eng): Quant experiment: R 5, I 7, C 4, E 5. But E includes infra validation + perf regression checks.
alex (Research): Agree with kevin. Also cost savings could free up Dedicated capacity budget.
sam (Product Ops): Proposal: carve out a "compliance sprint" for next two weeks to finish foundational controls (change mgmt, logging, incident playbooks), then run experiment in a seeded staging pool for 4 weeks. That gives sales a signal and keeps experiments moving.
maria (PM): I like that. Two questions: 1) does staging pool yield representative perf for quantized models? 2) how do we document isolation for SOC2 auditors?
kevin (Eng): Staging won't be identical but we can create a small Dedicated-like env with same instance types for the experiment. Adds ~10% infra cost but keeps production audit surface unchanged.
nisha (Security): For auditors we can document a carve-out: experiments run in a separate namespace with access controls and no customer data. Compliance team will draft the memo.
compliance-bot: Note: create compliance_ticket #C-421 and attach experiment isolation artifact before end of sprint.
maria (PM): Next steps: kevin to estimate infra delta + eng effort (2d), nisha to draft carve-out memo (3d), alex to scope experiment variants to 4 weeks, sam to update roadmap and RICE sheet. We'll present this hybrid plan to execs on Friday.
kevin (Eng): I can get estimates by EOD tomorrow.
nisha (Security): I'll draft the memo and ping legal for sign-off.
alex (Research): I'll cut the experiment to two prioritized variants to keep E low.
sam (Product Ops): I'll update the RICE spreadsheet and flag the deal impact.
maria (PM): Cool — aim is to avoid a binary choice. If execs want hard tradeoff, we'll default to SOC2-first for any customer-facing controls; experiments run in isolation. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
